blocks.prompt: 4. In how many ways can 5 couples sit on a round table if no two women are sitting together?
blocks.explanation:
5 couples = 5 men and 5 women at a round table, with no two women side by side.
Plan: seat the men first around the table, then put the women in the gaps between the men.
steps:
Given: 5 men and 5 women, round table, no two women adjacent.
To find: the number of seatings.
Method: Seat the men in a circle: \((5 - 1)!\) ways (Case-I). The 5 men make 5 gaps; put one woman in each gap: \(5!\) ways. Multiply (Fundamental Principle of Counting).

Seat the men
\[(5 - 1)! = 4! = 24\]
Why: The men alone form a circular arrangement; rotating them gives nothing new.

Seat the women in the gaps
\[5! = 120\]
Why: Between 5 men in a circle there are exactly 5 gaps. One woman in each gap keeps every two women apart. Once the men are seated the gaps are fixed (distinguishable), so the women are arranged in a line-like way: 5!.

Multiply
\[4! \times 5! = 24 \times 120 = 2880\]
Why: Each seating of the men can be combined with each placing of the women.

Check
\[\text{seats alternate: } M\,W\,M\,W \ldots\]
Why: With 5 men and 5 women and no two women together, the seats must alternate man, woman; a computer count of all such circular seatings also gives 2880.
